drhp.business: Shiva Cement, incorporated in Odisha in 1985 and a subsidiary of JSW Cement Limited (part of the JSW Group) since 2017, manufactures clinker and, from FY 2025-26, cement. Its manufacturing set-up comprises a clinkerisation plant, a cement grinding unit, a waste heat recovery power plant and captive limestone mines, with the clinker plant acting as a feeder to JSW Cement's eastern plants. risks.note: The MD&A's risk table states the cement sector is prone to supply-demand mismatches and faces fluctuations in its end-user sectors; with the industry adding roughly 50-55 MTPA of capacity in FY 2025-26 and a further 42-44 MTPA planned for FY 2026-27, regional oversupply can compress realisations for a small eastern-India producer.

Management flags that production is constrained by difficulties in sourcing sufficient, suitable-quality limestone; the Company mitigates through captive mines, auctioned mines, strategic inventory and specialist consultants for limestone deposit utilisation plans, but limestone availability is also cited industry-wide as a constraint on capacity addition.

The stated raw-material risk is continual margin erosion from volatile input costs, with rising global prices for coal and pet coke directly increasing manufacturing expenditure. Geopolitical tension in West Asia raised crude, pet coke, imported coal and diesel costs during the year; management says these pressures intensified late in FY 2025-26 and are expected to persist in the near term.
risks.risk: Input and energy cost volatility (coal, pet coke, fuel)

risks.note: The Company states the cement industry is highly exposed to logistical inefficiencies, with higher freight costs and inadequate critical infrastructure, particularly rail freight capacity and last-mile connectivity. Mitigation rests on the newly commissioned Sagra railway siding and the planned limestone belt conveyor, both still to prove savings.

The MD&A ratio commentary notes debt increased due to availment of a fresh term loan for project activity together with equity erosion, resulting in negative net worth for the year, and flags a DBS Bank term loan bullet payment of Rs 201.50 Cr due in March 2027 - a concentrated refinancing/repayment event against a loss-making year and rising finance cost.

The clinker plant is described as a key feeder to the Group's eastern plants; market presence is built on JSW Cement's established distribution network, the premium product is marketed by the parent as CHD Jalkavach, the 1 MTPA grinding capacity runs under an exclusive manufacturing partnership with group company Bhushan Power & Steel Limited, and CSR spending is borne by the holding company. Commercial terms and volumes are therefore substantially group-determined; the MD&A also notes there are no trade receivables as all sales are made against advance.
risks.risk: Dependence on the JSW group for offtake, distribution and operations

risks.note: Operations sit at one plant site at Village Telighana, Kutra, District Sundargarh, Odisha, with mines at Village Khatkurbahal, serving Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar - so any disruption at the site, its mines or in eastern-India demand hits the entire business, and the new capacity is a single grinding unit at Sambalpur.

FY 2026-27 earnings depend on maximising utilisation of the just-commissioned 1 MTPA grinding unit and on completing the belt conveyor project, which was still at pre-project activity stage; jobwork charges for operating the BPSL grinding unit already drove other expenses up 81.88%, so ramp shortfalls would leave the added cost without the volume.
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up of the new capacity
